rows.blind_basis: Direct mechanics definition and supplied Figure 12.3/12.4.
independently_derived_answer: A particle with sufficient inertia departs from a curving gas streamline and collides with the collector.
A particle following a streamline contacts the collector because its finite radius brings it within one particle radius of the surface.
released_reference: Inertial impaction occurs when suspended particles in a gas stream are unable to follow the curved streamlines around an obstacle because of their inertia; instead, they continue on a straighter path and collide with the obstacle, where they may be collected.

Interception occurs when a particle follows the gas streamline more closely, but still touches and is captured by the obstacle because the particle has a finite size. In interception, collection occurs due to geometric contact rather than because the particle departs strongly from the streamline.
